(1) `declared_rhythm` floors to `absent`: generation.trigger is an UNPOPULATED field, and an unpopulated field is not a measured negative. (2) `actual_trigger` is MEASURED and the discriminator is the Iceberg metadata tree, not the timestamps: 3 snapshot objects and 3 distinct write-commit uuids (04bf57a5-212f-4dde-b918-0bcbe175c32f, 46a8256d-e6ce-4ced-ad4f-c12269a08a12, a89e1c24-5a84-4d46-9dde-1dccd9358982) across 13 objects, so this table was written by THREE appends, not one. ⛔ SCOPED TO THE SURVIVING SET AND NOT BEYOND IT -- snapshot expiry and overwrite both converge on fewer surviving snapshots, so 'exactly three writes ever' would need the metadata log's snapshot HISTORY rather than its current head, and that is UNMEASURED. Three appends inside 11 minutes followed by 53 days of silence is a SESSION that ended, which is a different shape from a cadence that failed, and neither becomes the other by ageing. ⛔ WHY the session happened, and whether anyone intended it to repeat, is UNMEASURED.

key.evidence: ⛔ THE SAME UNRESOLVED IDENTITY QUESTION CARD 5 CARRIES, AND IT IS `inferred` FROM THIS SIDE TOO. MEASURED: two S3 homes exist under warehouse/globgrph/ whose table-name component is identically `cse_test`, differing only in uuid -- this one (bb57a916, written 2026-07-08) and card 5's (24458e6c, written 2026-07-08). Key sets disjoint. INFERRED: pyiceberg/Nessie assigns a NEW uuid-suffixed location per create_table and a namespace admits one table per name, so at most ONE of these homes is reachable by the catalog key and the other is an ORPHANED physical location. ⛔ UNMEASURED, AND IT IS THE DECIDING FACT: which home the catalog resolves to today. The Nessie catalog is not reachable from this seat, so this card CANNOT say which of the two is live and does not guess -- and it does NOT inherit card 5's reading, which is the same non-answer reached independently rather than a second vote. ⛔ ONE ORDERING FACT THIS SIDE ADDS, MEASURED: this home's writes (01:26:22) PRECEDE the sibling's (15:51:14) on the same day. That constrains WHICH would be the orphan under the create->drop->create reading -- an earlier location is the one a later create would strand -- but it does NOT settle it, because nothing measured here excludes the reverse order of catalog registration. Settling it needs one catalog.load_table((globgrph, 'cse_test')) read of its metadata location. NAMING the state is the carder's job; DECIDING it is the owner's.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: A true absence returns KeyCount=0 at rc=0 -- a failed retrieval returns a VALUE, not an error. And at THIS subject a wrong home does not even return 0: the same-named sibling returns a populated census
failure_mode.evidence: FOUR read-only probe classes, each a SEPARATE invocation, rc read UNPIPED. MEASURED: (1) true absence -> rc=0 out='0'; (2) wrong bucket -> rc=255 out='An error occurred (NoSuchBucket) when calling the ListObject', an ERROR not a zero; (3) wrong region -> rc=0 out='1'; (4) near-miss prefix, this home's own uuid tail mutated -> rc=0 out='0'. So a zero is produced by absence and by a wrong prefix, and NOT by a wrong bucket. ⛔ THE FIFTH CLASS -- a missing s3:ListBucket -- WAS NOT EXERCISED and may also return a zero; that unexercised class is the SOLE ground on which distinguishable_from_true_negative is `no` at basis `inferred`. ⛔ AND AT THIS SUBJECT THE SHARPEST FAILURE IS NOT A ZERO: because the same-named sibling home is real and populated, a home confused between the two returns a healthy KeyCount=1 and a full census while the card describes the wrong table. That class is caught structurally by refuse_sibling_confusion() at build time, which RAISED nothing here because the two censuses differ on every axis measured (see the location row).

verdict.why: NOT LOAD-BEARING on the evidence gathered here: an isolated test-harness table whose SURVIVING objects were written by 3 appends inside 11 minutes on 2026-07-08 with no later surviving write, 53 days stale at carding. It is carded because it EXISTS in the manifest and occupies a real S3 home, not because anything was shown to read it. QUALIFIED, and these are the qualifications: the materializer is `inferred` -- the invocations were never found and the partition-spec match identifies a writer CLASS, not a run; the `key` row carries an UNRESOLVED identity question, since two homes share the table name `cse_test` and this seat cannot reach the Nessie catalog to say which one it addresses, so one of the two may be an orphaned location and this card does not claim which; coverage spans the OBJECT plane only and NO row was read; and whether any consumer reads this table is UNMEASURED. ⛔ THIS CARD DOES NOT CLASSIFY THE TABLE AS DEBT AND DOES NOT PROPOSE DROPPING IT: --drop permits it, but a permission is not a recommendation. Naming the state is the carder's job; deciding it is the owner's.
